issues.legal_issue: Credible eyewitness testimony can establish a criminal conviction even when the witnesses are related to the deceased and no independent eyewitness is examined.
material_facts: The prosecution eyewitnesses included two injured witnesses whose presence at the incident was supported by their injuries and prompt medical examination.
The injured informant’s report was recorded shortly after the incident and named the accused and their specific roles.
The eyewitness account was consistent with the report and the medical evidence, including the evidence of firearm injuries.

The deceased’s relatives were naturally present because they had accompanied him in connection with the court-directed delivery of possession, and the young daughter’s presence with them was not unusual.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness evidence proved the prosecution case, and the witnesses’ relationship to the deceased and the absence of independent witnesses did not require rejection of their testimony.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the reliability of the eyewitnesses in light of their presence, prompt reporting, injuries, and consistency with medical evidence; relationship to the deceased alone did not make their evidence unreliable. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and eyewitnesses_witnessed_the_occurrence and (injured_witnesses_promptly_examined or witnesses_naturally_present) and prompt_report_identified_roles and eyewitness_account_corresponded_with_medical_evidence

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered after a criminal trial.
predicates.eyewitnesses_witnessed_the_occurrence: Witnesses testified that they saw the events resulting in the victim’s death.
predicates.injured_witnesses_promptly_examined: Witnesses who said they saw the occurrence had injuries and were medically examined shortly afterwards.
predicates.witnesses_naturally_present: The witnesses had a circumstance-based reason to be present at the scene.
predicates.prompt_report_identified_roles: A report made shortly after the occurrence identified the accused and described their roles.
predicates.eyewitness_account_corresponded_with_med: The eyewitness account was consistent with the medical evidence concerning the victim’s injuries.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a criminal conviction rests on eyewitnesses who witnessed the occurrence, and their presence, prompt reporting, and account are supported by the stated circumstances and medical evidence, the eyewitness evidence supports the conviction.

issues.legal_issue: An accused who knowingly participates in restraining a victim so that an armed participant can shoot the victim may be held liable for murder as part of the common object or common intention.
material_facts: Two accused held the deceased’s arms to immobilize him while another accused fired a countrymade firearm at him.
The court found that the accused knew that the shooter was carrying a firearm and that the restraint facilitated the shooting.
One of the accused who restrained the deceased exhorted the shooter to kill him.
issues.conclusion: The participation of the accused who restrained the deceased supported their convictions for murder with the shooter under the principles of common object and common intention.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principles of common object under Section 149 and common intention under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, finding that the accused knew of the firearm and actively facilitated the killing; the exhortation further supported the finding against the accused who gave it. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_case_involving_murder: The proceeding concerned a charge arising from a victim’s death caused by an attack.
predicates.accused_restrained_victim_to_facilitate_: The accused held or restrained the victim in a way that facilitated an attack by another participant.
predicates.accused_knew_participant_carried_firearm: The accused knew that another participant was carrying a firearm when the victim was restrained.

issues.definition: In a murder case, when an accused knowingly restrains the victim to facilitate an armed participant’s attack, the accused may be held jointly liable for the murder.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to examine the investigating officer does not by itself invalidate a criminal trial or require the prosecution case to fail.
material_facts: The investigating officer was not examined at trial.
The eyewitness evidence clearly established the accused’s involvement and conformed to the prompt report and the medical evidence.
The court assessed the claimed prejudice in the circumstances of the case rather than treating non-examination as automatically fatal.
issues.conclusion: The investigating officer’s non-examination did not require the prosecution case to fail in this case.
issues.legal_principle: Whether an accused suffered prejudice from non-examination of the investigating officer depends on the facts; there is no universal rule that the omission per se vitiates a criminal trial. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_trial and investigating_officer_not_examined and prosecution_evidence_clearly_established_involvement and evidence_conformed_to_report_and_medical_evidence and specific_prejudice_not_established

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding was a criminal trial of accused persons.
predicates.investigating_officer_not_examined: The investigating officer did not testify at trial.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_clearly_established: The evidence presented by the prosecution clearly established the accused’s involvement.
predicates.evidence_conformed_to_report_and_medical: The prosecution evidence was consistent with the prompt report and the medical evidence.
predicates.specific_prejudice_not_established: The circumstances did not establish prejudice sufficient to undermine the prosecution case.

issues.definition: When an investigating officer is not examined at a criminal trial but the prosecution evidence clearly establishes involvement, accords with the report and medical evidence, and no sufficient specific prejudice is established, the omission does not invalidate the trial.

issues.legal_issue: A trial court should not admit the entire police case diary as an exhibit.
material_facts: The trial court allowed the entire case diary to be exhibited.
The Supreme Court found that the diary should not have been allowed to be exhibited, while also finding that the eyewitness evidence independently established the accused’s involvement.
issues.conclusion: The trial court should not have allowed the entire case diary to be exhibited, but that error did not cause the prosecution case to fail in this matter.
issues.legal_principle: Section 172(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that the police diary is not to be used as evidence in the case. The court did not rely on an earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding was a criminal trial.
predicates.entire_police_case_diary_admitted_as_exh: The trial court admitted the entire police case diary as an exhibit.

issues.definition: When a criminal trial court admits the entire police case diary as an exhibit, it should not admit the diary as evidence.
